notes.text: The page introduces a tree Gamma=(S,A,R), vertices S, edges A and the incidence relation. The bracketed remark contains A into P_2(S) and S to P(A), then an injectivity statement with the drawn two-vertex one-edge graph as its stated exception. The visibly decorated left end of the second arrow remains uncertain.

The author introduces families U_s and E_a and defines X by their two displayed disjoint unions. The graph is reproduced as two filled vertices and one edge without arrowheads. There are no additional figure labels.

The text cuts the tree at a_0, names Gamma prime and Gamma double-prime, gives a binary decomposition, and writes separate coproduct formulas for X prime and X double-prime. The second lower edge index visibly has an open c-shaped form; the summand remains E_a. The following connective is avec and the intersection is written E_{a_0}.

The lower text calls the decomposition propre and writes two inequalities. The first smallest index has an ascending b-like stroke, which is retained with 0 as an alternative. The next prose sentence and the final parenthesized criterion concern sommet-bout and U_s nonempty. Both equivalence abbreviations are visibly sss. No mathematical correction was introduced.

The parallel indices and repeated a_0 were considered as reading cues only. They did not decide the open c|a in the second coproduct or b|0 in the first inequality. The graph and injectivity prose did not decide the overwritten second arrow. No proof, independent re-proof or computation was performed.

No title, date, authorial question mark or explicit check instruction is visible. The number 27 is in faint pencil at the lower left and is retained as an archive sheet-number comment. H's note about A prime and A double-prime is editorial text without a manuscript counterpart.

notes.text: The page is a handwritten working sheet. No title or date is visible. A small pencil 27 sits at bottom left and is retained as an archive-sheet comment; no author page number is separately supplied.

The opening introduces Gamma=(S,A,R), describes S and A with the abbreviated ens, and describes R with an accent-uncertain form of relation d’incidence. The bracketed passage contains two displayed-in-prose maps to handwritten P forms. The second arrow’s left terminal remains uncertain.

The author’s discussion of injectivity ends with a graph of two filled vertices joined by one plain segment. Both endpoints and the absence of arrowheads were read directly on the page; the graph is reproduced with tikzcd.

The author introduces (U_s) and (E_a), then writes a coproduct expression for X. The next paragraph names a_0, uses the phrase “coupé en a_0”, and writes Gamma prime and Gamma double-prime, followed by X prime and X double-prime expressions. Visible overwritten forms are preserved.

The author writes avec beside the intersection equality. H’s note about membership of a_0 in A prime/A double-prime has no handwritten counterpart in the blank interval. It is not added to the transcription and was not treated as an author’s doubt.

The lower prose uses the quoted word “propre”, then the abbreviation sss twice, and leads to the asterisk-labelled sentence mentioning a sommet-bout and the inequality U_s not equal to the crossed-oval empty-set sign. No explicit proof check, question, date, or authorial caution is visible on this page.

Mathematical context affected only the list of alternatives: the repeated E_a supports the alternative a for the open c-shaped last coproduct index, and the repeated a_0 supports the alternative 0 for the b-shaped first inequality index. The transcription retains c and b as the respective primary ink readings. The following two families support the live plural Soient; its original t is independently visible. notes.text: The opening introduces a tree Gamma=(S,A,R), naming S, A and R in that order. The author writes A with a clean hooked right arrow to a decorated P_2(S), followed by the S-to-P(A) expression whose left-end arrow decoration remains uncertain. The subsequent source words call it an application and refer to injectivity and the two-vertex one-edge graph. These words influenced attention to the map sign but did not settle its crowded strokes.

Two indexed families (U_s) and (E_a) are introduced, followed by the displayed coproduct expression for X. The one-edge graph is represented by two filled dots and a single solid connector without arrowheads.

The author refers to the two components of Gamma “coupé en a_0”, then writes a binary decomposition X=X prime union X double prime. The definitions of the two parts occupy successive display rows, followed by avec and the displayed intersection E_{a_0}. The final coproduct index is visibly open like c, while the summand retains the a subscript. Both observed forms are retained with the stated uncertainty.

The paragraph uses the author’s quotation marks around “propre”, two occurrences of sss, and two inequalities. The lower character in the first inequality has a b-like stem, despite the earlier and neighbouring zero forms. The page ends with a parenthesized ambiguous label and the author’s sentence about a sommet-bout and U_s. This is a source description; no proof of the stated criterion was checked.

No date, title, explicit author question, or author proof-check annotation is visible on this sheet. The light pencil 27 in the lower left is retained as archive numbering, without a manuscript-page macro. The doubts retained in this return belong to the reading, not to explicit question marks by the author.

Mathematical cues considered during reading were the repeated family indices, the first a_0 and the neighbouring E_{a_0}, and the prose application/injectivity wording. These cues were not used to change contradictory visible strokes. The editorial H note about A prime and A double prime has no visible manuscript counterpart and is excluded from the page transcription.
